overview: The Medford Community Preservation Committee evaluates applications and recommends allocations of Community Preservation Act funds across affordable housing, historic preservation, and open space and recreation projects. The committee has been meeting regularly across the 2022-2023, 2024-2025, and 2026-2027 terms to review grant submissions, manage annual budgets, and update local application policies. Over this span, it has recommended funding for municipal building rehabilitations, public park and school athletic improvements, cemetery preservation, and housing initiatives. As of October 2026, the committee is reviewing initial applications for the fiscal year 2027 funding round, including proposals for rental assistance, City Hall exterior repairs, athletic court renovations, and tree plantings.

threads.name: Affordable housing support
threads.summary: In August 2023, the committee approved an $800,000 funding request for the Medford Housing Authority's Walkland Court redevelopment project. The committee later increased its FY25 budget set-aside for affordable housing to 15% and received early briefings on the newly formed Affordable Housing Trust Fund. It subsequently recommended $250,000 in seed money for the Affordable Housing Trust and $100,000 for the ABCD Medford Move-in Program in late 2024. In 2026, the committee monitored updates on Walkling Court and trust activities, and in October 2026 took up an FY27 application from ABCD requesting $117,043 for rental assistance.

threads.name: Historic cemetery restoration
threads.summary: Master planning and preservation for Oak Grove and Cross Street cemeteries were identified as priorities during the March 2024 annual hearing. In late 2024 and early 2025, the committee recommended design funds for Oak Grove Cemetery buildings and $5,000 for veteran headstone restorations at Cross Street Cemetery. DPW updates in late 2025 outlined multi-million-dollar preservation alternatives for Oak Grove structures alongside an application to restore its Angel of Victory and Peace fountain. In September 2026, the committee approved $167,800 to restore the fountain and $126,500 for Phase 2 monuments and perimeter wall repairs at Cross Street Cemetery.

threads.name: Church exterior and accessibility restorations
threads.summary: In 2024, the committee reviewed applications from Unitarian Universalist Church, St. Francis Church, and Shiloh Baptist Church, referring an off-cycle request from Shiloh back to the regular cycle. In December 2024, it recommended $99,000 for siding repairs at Unitarian Universalist Church and $400,000 for ADA improvements at Shiloh Baptist Church. By mid-2025, the committee began developing stricter guidelines for funding private properties while reviewing Shiloh's subsequent stained glass requests. The committee ultimately approved $10,000 for the Unitarian Universalist Church's Osgood House repairs in July 2026 and $150,000 for Phase 2 window restoration at Shiloh Baptist Church in September 2026.

threads.name: City Hall facility improvements
threads.summary: The committee initiated discussions on municipal preservation needs including City Hall windows in early 2024, followed by presentations for ADA bathroom upgrades and City Council chamber window restorations. In December 2024, the committee approved a $322,500 funding recommendation to restore council chamber windows with historical documentation conditions. Further municipal requests emerged in 2026, leading to October 2026 reviews of an FY27 proposal seeking $300,000 for limestone facade repairs and building assessments, as well as $51,000 for ADA drinking fountain replacements.

threads.name: Park and recreation enhancements
threads.summary: The committee supported recreational amenities across multiple parks, recommending Phase 2 funds for Carr Park, $526,000 to reconstruct Playstead Park tennis courts, and shade installation at Riverside Plaza. Additional contingency funding was requested and approved in 2025 and 2026 for the Riverside Plaza shade structure and the Playstead digital scoreboard. In September 2026, the committee approved $432,000 for Tufts Park Field 2 lighting improvements. In October 2026, the committee heard a new FY27 request for $264,000 to resurface Victory Park athletic courts.

threads.name: Condon Shell improvements
threads.summary: In August 2023, the committee approved a $3,276 small grant for electrical outlets and safety lighting at the Condon Shell. An application for expanded app-controlled field and walkway lighting was presented in late 2024 and approved for $98,285 in December 2024. In October 2026, the Recreation Director requested permission to pivot $50,000 from a previous Tufts Field allocation to address a Condon Shell lighting budget shortfall caused by higher material costs and footing replacements.

threads.name: School campus and playground facilities
threads.summary: The committee approved $400,000 in August 2023 for Phase 2 construction of the McGlynn School universal playground, followed by smaller grants in June 2024 for McGlynn and Roberts schools and district bicycle infrastructure. Updates confirmed the near-completion of the $2.8 million McGlynn playground in mid-2024. In July 2026, the committee discussed potential long-term CPA funding for non-reimbursable elements of the new Medford High School project, establishing a dedicated subcommittee to formulate a multi-year funding and bonding strategy.

threads.name: Urban forestry and environmental inventories
threads.summary: In May 2024, the committee approved a $5,000 small grant for Trees Medford to inventory 1,000 trees in public parks to assist municipal GIS mapping and vulnerability tracking. The work on park canopy health reappeared in the FY27 application cycle, where the Department of Public Works presented a $75,000 funding request in October 2026 to plant new trees and replace losses from pest infestations.

periods.narrative: The committee established budget projections with conservative state matching estimates and recommended major project allocations for public housing pre-development and the McGlynn playground.

The committee updated its annual preservation plans, raised the housing allocation target, and recommended over $2 million for municipal, historic, park, and housing initiatives while revising small grant rules.
The committee approved emergency repairs and cemetery and lighting projects, initiated planning for high school project funding, and commenced review of FY27 applications.
